observations.statement: F3-398 is an accepted GUI-related requirement owned by Plans/FinalGUISpec.md.

User-facing and canonical naming is PRD Builder and Planning Wizard; Requirements Doc Builder, Chain Wizard, and Plan Wizard are retired from active product prose, UI, commands, events, and contracts.

PRD Builder supports conversation-first intake without source documents, upload ingestion into a normalized PRD/PRD Pack, and combining uploads with conversation at any time; questioning is batched, reuses ledger answers, avoids repetition, and prioritizes material answers.
The primary PRD has an explicit section inventory, and the default workspace emphasizes that PRD while exposing supporting constraints, questions, traceability, and quality/readiness views.
Approve PRD for Planning Wizard creates an immutable handoff snapshot, and Planning Wizard consumes a specific approved version instead of mutable editor state.

Selection and source actions create durable version-and-anchor-bound context or annotations; invalidated highlights become stale, retain original text, attempt evidence-backed remapping, and ask the user only when safe remapping is impossible.
PRD Builder exposes Ready, Ready with Warnings, and Blocked using listed readiness inputs, and accepted warnings carry into Planning Wizard.

Planning Wizard derives a dynamic topic graph and permits controller-driven add, split, merge, rename, defer, reopen, reorder, and impact operations while recording reasons, sources, dependencies, origins, and invalidations.

Dependency-changing decisions propagate typed impacts and stale/recompile/reaudit markers; a topic becomes Ready only after successful conversion and audit, remains reviewable/reopenable, and does not require confirmation after every topic.
Planning intake can attach local directories, Git repositories, optional GitHub repositories, or remote SSH roots and records host, path, repository identity, currentness, and permissions.

Testing capability policy exists globally and per project with inheritance/override, carries an effective snapshot across Planning Wizard, Plan Compile, Executor, and Orchestrator, and assigns Auto, On, or Off per capability family.
The default testing visibility policy exposes meaningful headed or visual sessions when possible, with explicit web and native examples of visible interaction, evidence, and pass/fail surfaces.

Approve And Build is the exact final label; local success switches to Orchestrator Plan Compile, and an unreconciled publication or compile identity uses a pending shell that later binds without duplication.

Planning Wizard is one workspace with a collapsible plan/project parent, topic and audit/repair children, topic map, Assistant Chat, live preview, readiness/source panels, twelve named topic-card states, and progress details for long-running stages.

Plan Compile displays compilation/handoff evidence and owns that progress; after BuildStarted, execution views own dispatch and implementation activity while Plan Compile becomes a historical launch view with Open Build.

The command set is required to define permission, enablement, disabled reason, idempotency, stale-projection behavior, receipt effect, and recovery; only initial approval forces navigation, while later transitions use status and Open Build actions.

F3-398 acceptance is expressed as source-atom preservation, preservation of exact lineage material, and prohibition on creating build artifacts; its named validation surfaces are plan-index and bootstrap-ledger validators.

F3-399 routes seven discovery GUI consumers through DiscoveryService and requires them to expose an extensive state set including stale, fallback, denied, hidden-by-policy, unsupported, and backpressure conditions.
Discovery GUI surfaces preserve shared ranking unless a local sort/filter is disclosed; rank explanations are coarse and may not reveal private history or blocked-path details.

F3-399 declares upstream dependencies and downstream consumers, acceptance criteria for naming, state distinction, disclosure, and no-leak explanations, plus plan validation and future parity/state tests.
Both the F3-398 and F3-399 node-compile hints explicitly prohibit creating WorkNodes or NodeSeeds.

candidate_findings.title: F3-398 behavioral acceptance is not executable in this window
candidate_findings.statement: The accepted requirement defines extensive user-visible, stateful, and cross-surface behavior, but its acceptance criteria check lineage preservation and non-creation of build artifacts, while its validators check plan indexing and the source ledger. No acceptance oracle in the assigned core verifies the specified GUI behavior, state transitions, handoff, policy propagation, or recovery.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can satisfy the listed acceptance and validation surfaces while materially diverging from the canonical product contract.

candidate_findings.title: Per-command contract values are absent
candidate_findings.statement: The core says each named command defines permission, enablement, disabled reason, idempotency, stale-projection behavior, receipt effect, and recovery, but it does not supply those values or a per-command matrix.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders must invent security gates, retry/idempotency behavior, stale-state handling, receipts, and recovery, risking inconsistent commands and duplicate or unauthorized effects.

candidate_findings.title: PRD readiness outcomes lack a deterministic decision model
candidate_findings.statement: Ready, Ready with Warnings, and Blocked are said to be based on six input categories, but the assigned core gives no thresholds, precedence, conflict-resolution rules, required-section definition, warning-acceptance authority, or transition rules.
candidate_findings.impact: The same PRD can receive different readiness outcomes across implementations, and approval eligibility or warning carry-forward cannot be tested deterministically.

candidate_findings.title: Topic lifecycle and graph mutation semantics are incomplete
candidate_findings.statement: The core lists graph mutations, impact markers, and twelve GUI states but does not define transition guards, legal combinations, dependency-type vocabulary, merge/split dependency rewriting, concurrent edit ordering, rollback, or the conditions that clear stale, impacted, reopened, deferred, and blocked states.
candidate_findings.impact: Controller and GUI implementations can disagree about topic authority and readiness, leave invalid topics apparently usable, or lose dependency impacts during mutations.

candidate_findings.title: Anchor remapping safety is left to builders
candidate_findings.statement: The core requires evidence-backed and safe remapping but does not define anchor identity, matching inputs, confidence thresholds, multi-match disambiguation, concurrent-revision handling, persistence schema, or an auditable reason for declaring remapping impossible.
candidate_findings.impact: Annotations may silently bind to incorrect text or prompt users inconsistently after document revisions.

candidate_findings.title: Testing-policy authority and snapshot resolution are underspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The core names global inheritance, project override, effective snapshots, and Auto installation within authority, but it does not define per-capability merge precedence, snapshot creation/version/refresh timing, the authority source, consent boundaries, installation failure handling, or behavior when On remains unavailable.
candidate_findings.impact: The same settings can authorize different installations or test behavior across Planning Wizard, Plan Compile, Executor, and Orchestrator, creating security and reproducibility risks.

candidate_findings.title: Visible-verification conditions have no deterministic fallback
candidate_findings.statement: The show_when_possible contract depends on undefined judgments such as meaningful, supported, available, and permitted, and it does not state what user-visible fallback, reason, freshness indicator, or evidence minimum is required when a live surface cannot be shown.
candidate_findings.impact: A compliant-looking implementation may hide verification or expose materially different evidence without explaining why, undermining the stated visibility guarantee.

candidate_findings.title: Approve And Build reconciliation lacks a complete durable protocol
candidate_findings.statement: The core requires a pending shell to bind to a durable compile identity without duplication, but does not define the approval correlation key, what local success means, publication/identity timeout and failure states, restart persistence, competing approvals, cancellation, or retry behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Crashes, retries, or delayed publication can yield duplicate compile runs, orphaned pending shells, or an approval that never reaches a recoverable build view.

candidate_findings.title: The never-stalled progress guarantee is not measurable
candidate_findings.statement: Long-running work must show stage, counts, pass, and status so the UI never appears stalled, but the core defines neither update cadence nor stale-progress threshold, heartbeat behavior, count semantics, unavailable estimates, or failure/cancellation presentation.
candidate_findings.impact: A frozen or misleading progress surface can still claim conformance, and users cannot distinguish slow work from stalled work.

candidate_findings.title: Attached-source validation and permission semantics are absent
candidate_findings.statement: The core lists local, Git, GitHub, and SSH sources and metadata to record, but does not define identity canonicalization, credential/permission verification, currentness calculation, refresh timing, unreachable-source behavior, path validation, or repository-change handling.
candidate_findings.impact: Planning may consume stale or misidentified sources, disclose inaccessible paths, or behave inconsistently across source types.

candidate_findings.title: Discovery states are enumerated without a state machine
candidate_findings.statement: F3-399 exposes many distinct discovery states plus settings and reset, but the assigned core does not define precedence, coexistence, transitions, retry/cancellation, backpressure recovery, stale-versus-fallback ranking, reset effects, or the output contract for each state.
candidate_findings.impact: The seven consumers can render contradictory states, leak results in denied or hidden conditions, or recover differently from the same service event.

candidate_findings.title: Discovery ranking and no-leak acceptance lack a present oracle
candidate_findings.statement: The core requires ranking preservation, disclosed local reordering, and coarse no-leak explanations, but does not define disclosure placement/timing, a closed explanation vocabulary, parity tolerances, or current executable tests; the named parity and state tests are explicitly future.
candidate_findings.impact: Undisclosed reranking or privacy-revealing explanations may pass current validation and differ across consumers.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Current product naming and retirement of Requirements Doc Builder, Chain Wizard, and Plan Wizard are explicit.
Users are explicitly allowed to combine upload and conversation without restarting, and the negative constraints forbid a permanent mode choice or repeated giant questionnaires.
The PRD-to-planning handoff is explicitly immutable and version-specific rather than mutable editor state.
The stale-anchor contract explicitly preserves original selected text and limits user interruption to cases where safe remapping is impossible.
A topic requires successful conversion and audit to become Ready, and the negative constraints prohibit leaving it Ready after a material dependency change.
Off explicitly prohibits capability use and installation and does not imply a verification pass.
Backend audit/subagent detail is explicitly nested or expandable rather than made into separate top-level app surfaces.
Compilation/handoff and post-BuildStarted WorkNode execution ownership are explicitly separated.
Approve And Build intentionally performs the initial navigation, while later state changes must not forcibly move the user.
Hidden-by-policy is explicitly distinct from no-results.
Shared discovery ranking order, disclosure of local reordering, and non-disclosure of private history and blocked-path details are explicit.
The compile hints explicitly prevent this planning material from creating WorkNodes or NodeSeeds.

unknowns.statement: The exact readiness decision table, precedence among readiness inputs, and authority to accept warnings are not stated in the assigned core.
The identity, confidence threshold, and disambiguation rules that make an annotation remap safe are not stated.
The typed topic-dependency vocabulary and mapping from dependency changes to stale_due_to_dependency_change, stale_due_to_new_scope, requires_recompile, or requires_reaudit are not stated.
How source permissions and currentness are computed, refreshed, and surfaced for local, GitHub, and SSH sources is not stated.
The authority provider for Auto installation and the durable versioning/refresh rules for the effective testing-policy snapshot are not stated.
The correlation identity, persistence boundary, and restart/retry protocol connecting approval, PlanApproved publication, pending launch, and PlanCompileRun are not stated.
The units, monotonicity, update cadence, and stale threshold for progress counts, assignment counts, findings fixed, and current pass are not stated.
The command-specific permission, idempotency, stale-projection, receipt, and recovery values are not stated.
The precedence and transition rules among discovery loading, warming, stale, fallback, denied, no-results, hidden-by-policy, disabled, unsupported, and backpressure states are not stated.
The exact local-sort disclosure UI and the executable parity/no-leak oracle are not stated; only future tests are named.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_quote: status: accepted
owner_doc: Plans/FinalGUISpec.md

The finished-product feature formerly called Requirements Doc Builder is named PRD Builder everywhere in user-facing UI and canonical product documentation. The canonical product name is Planning Wizard; Chain Wizard and Plan Wizard are stale names that must be retired from active product prose, UI, commands, events, and contracts.

A user with no source documents can start in PRD Builder chat; the agent asks discovery questions, updates the PRD ledger every turn, and continuously renders the PRD projection. A user can upload existing requirements material and have PRD Builder preserve, parse, extract, reconcile, and normalize it into the standard PRD and PRD Pack. Uploads and conversation may be combined at any time in one PRD Builder workspace so users can clarify, correct, extend, override, and source newly introduced requirements without restarting.
Ask questions in digestible batches, use existing ledger
answers before asking, avoid repetition, and prefer questions whose answers materially change the PRD.

The primary PRD contains Summary, Problem or Opportunity, Goals, Users or Actors, Scope, Non-Goals, Functional Requirements, Non-Functional Requirements, UX Expectations, Data or Integration or Environment Constraints, Acceptance Criteria, Assumptions, Risks and Dependencies, Open Questions, and Source Notes.

The default workspace emphasizes one primary PRD while exposing supporting assumptions and constraints, open questions, source traceability, and quality/readiness views without making users manage many equal documents.

The PRD Builder final action is labeled Approve PRD for Planning Wizard and creates the immutable handoff snapshot; the Planning Wizard consumes a specific approved version rather than mutable editor state.

Highlight, comment, ask, request change, replace, remove, move to non-goal, mark unclear, show source, and challenge
  source actions create durable context or annotation records bound to document version and text anchors.
When revisions invalidate a highlighted span, mark the anchor stale, attempt evidence-backed remapping, preserve the original selected text, and ask the user only when safe remapping is impossible.

PRD Builder exposes Ready, Ready with Warnings, and Blocked based on source extraction, required sections, blocking conflicts, annotations, quality findings, and approval-snapshot ability; accepted warnings carry into Planning Wizard.

Planning Wizard derives an initial topic graph from the input pack, project/repository context, work intent, risk, and known defaults rather than enforcing a fixed list of sections. The controller can add, split, merge, rename, defer, reopen, reorder, and mark topics impacted, recording the reason, source refs, dependencies, user-visible origin, and resulting invalidations.

A later decision that changes a prior topic''s assumptions or outputs marks affected topic drafts stale_due_to_dependency_change, stale_due_to_new_scope, or requires_recompile/requires_reaudit and propagates impact through typed topic dependencies.

A topic becomes Ready after successful conversion and audit; users may review or reopen any topic, but ordinary flow does not require a user confirmation after every topic. Final planning review uses the shared live document preview, selection context menu, comments, source inspection, challenge, targeted revision, and annotation status system used by PRD Builder.
Planning intake can attach an existing local directory, Git repository, optional GitHub repository, or remote SSH host and project root, recording host, path, repository identity, currentness,
and permissions.

Testing capability policy is configurable globally and per project, with project settings inheriting or overriding global values and the effective policy snapshot carried into Planning Wizard, Plan Compile, Executor, and Orchestrator.

Each testing capability family supports Auto, On, and Off: Auto discovers and selects or installs within authority; On is required and blocks or asks for authority when unavailable; Off prohibits use and installation for that capability without implying a pass.

Settings cover online capability research, automated installation, built-in browser, headed browser, visible browser automation, hot reload, live preview, desktop GUI testing, simulator or emulator, physical device, screenshot or visual comparison, accessibility, API or contract, database, console or network, performance, and security testing.

The default testing visibility policy is show_when_possible: when a meaningful headed or visual
  surface exists, expose the active test session rather than hiding all verification in background logs.

For web work, open the built-in browser or headed browser view and visibly show navigation, clicks, form input, assertions, screenshots, console and network evidence, and pass/fail progression when supported. For Swift and other native work, show the appropriate live preview, hot-reload surface, simulator, emulator, device stream, application window, interaction trace, screenshots, and relevant logs when available and permitted.

The Planning Wizard final approval button and command label is exactly Approve And Build. After Approve And Build succeeds locally, the application automatically switches to the Orchestrator page and opens the Plan Compile tab so the user sees launch reconciliation and compilation starting.

If PlanApproved publication or PlanCompileRun identity has not yet reconciled, the Plan Compile tab shows a pending launch
  shell tied to the approval command and then binds to the durable compile identity without creating a duplicate.

Planning Wizard GUI shows a collapsible parent named for the plan or project with child topic threads, dynamically added topics, final integration, final review, and attached audit/repair activity. The user remains in one Planning Wizard workspace with topic map, active Assistant Chat panel, live plan preview, source/annotation/readiness panels, and bounded backend child threads loaded as selected. Topic cards represent not_started, active, ledger_syncing, ledger_synced, compiling, auditing, repairing, ready, impacted, reopened, deferred, and blocked, with clear dependency and origin badges. Long-running topic conversion, audit, repair, final integration, and final audit display active stage, progress counts, assignment counts, findings fixed, current pass, and user-relevant status so the interface never appears stalled.   Audit and repair children are attached under their topic or final Plan Pack and summarized in activity/progress views; detailed agent traces and evidence may be expanded without cluttering the default thread tree.

Orchestrator Plan Compile tab shows immutable source pack, current stage, stage timeline, subagent assignments, PlanUnit coverage, NodeSeed candidates, WorkGraph status, WorkNodeRequest count, testing/model/source-control readiness, audit/repair cycles, blockers, receipts, and handoff status. Plan Compile tab owns compilation and handoff progress; after BuildStarted, Orchestrator execution views own WorkNode dispatch, code changes, live testing, repairs, safe points, and completion while Plan Compile remains a historical launch view with an Open Build action.

Commands for topic navigation, reopen, defer, annotation revision, approve PRD, Approve And Build, pause, cancel, resume, retry, inspect blocker, inspect evidence, inspect assignment, request
  bounded recompile, and open resulting build define permission, enablement, disabled reason, idempotency, stale-projection behavior, receipt effect, and recovery.
Approve And Build intentionally navigates to Orchestrator Plan Compile, but later transitions present strong Open Build and status actions rather than forcibly moving the user whenever state changes.

gui_related: true
gui_classification_reason: Includes user-visible GUI/workspace/command/projection behavior.

acceptance_criteria:
- The live owner doc preserves every source atom listed in source_atom_ids without treating the ledger as canonical product prose.
- Exact tokens, negative constraints, owner hints, and accepted corrections remain available to future audits through this PlanUnit.
- No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, GoalRuns, implementation files, generated governance artifacts, or production build tasks are created by this compile.

validation_surfaces:
- python3 scripts/pm-plan-index.py validate
- python3 scripts/pm-bootstrap-ledger-validate.py Plans/ledgers/v2/pldg-20260618-001-prd-planning-wizard

node_compile_hint:
  mode: canonical_planunit_from_bootstrap_ledger
  create_worknodes: false
  create_nodeseeds: false

GUI path/context discovery surfaces route through the shared DiscoveryService while preserving established user-facing names and shortcuts. Quick Open, command palette fuzzy search, Search path narrowing, Assistant Chat file mentions, File Manager type-ahead, Planning Wizard source picker, and PRD Builder source picker expose loading, indexing/warming, stale, fallback, denied, no-results, hidden-by-policy, disabled, unsupported, over-budget/backpressure, rank explanation, disclosed local sort/filter, settings, and reset states.

GUI surfaces preserve DiscoveryService ranking order unless they disclose a local sort/filter, and coarse rank explanations may show path match, recent in this project, current context, stale cache, or fallback without exposing raw private frecency/query/open history or blocked path details.

acceptance_criteria:
  - GUI discovery surfaces preserve established command names and shortcuts.
  - Hidden-by-policy is distinct from ordinary no-results.
  - Local sort/filter behavior is disclosed when it changes visible order.
  - Rank explanations are coarse and no-leak.

validation_surfaces:
  - python3 scripts/pm-plan-index.py validate
  - Future GUI/agent ranking parity tests.
  - Future GUI stale/fallback/denied/no-results/hidden-by-policy state tests.
node_compile_hint: {mode: gui_discovery_consumer_contract, create_worknodes: false, create_nodeseeds: false}

- Do not leave a topic marked Ready after a material dependency change.
- Do not treat Off as successful verification.
- Do not present every backend subagent or audit thread as a separate top-level app surface.
- Do not mix ongoing WorkNode execution into Plan Compile stage progress.

negative_constraints:
  - Do not conflate hidden-by-policy with ordinary no-results.
  - Do not rename established GUI commands or shortcuts as part of discovery routing.
  - Do not run an undisclosed second ranking pass that changes shared DiscoveryService order.

- Do not preserve Requirements Doc Builder as a current product feature name except in explicitly historical migration notes.
- Do not use Chain Wizard or Plan Wizard as current terminology.

- Do not force users to choose permanently between upload and chat.
- Do not re-ask answered questions or overwhelm the user with one giant questionnaire.
